summary.title: OpenCV Text Detection (EAST text detector)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to run OpenCV's EAST deep learning text detector in Python to find text in natural scene images, with a walkthrough of the code and its limitations.
keywords: heuristic text detection vs deep learning
takeaways: EAST is an end-to-end deep learning scene text detector that OpenCV supports from version 3.4.2 and OpenCV 4, reported to run at about 13 FPS on 720p images.
Natural scene text is hard because of sensor noise, viewing angle, blur, lighting, resolution, reflective and non-planar surfaces, and unknown layout.

The pipeline loads the frozen EAST model, reads the 'feature_fusion/Conv_7/Sigmoid' score and 'feature_fusion/concat_3' geometry layers, decodes boxes above a confidence threshold, then applies non-maxima suppression.
Input width and height must be multiples of 32; the author's Python version cannot produce rotated boxes and uses imutils NMS because cv2.dnn.NMSBoxes failed in their OpenCV 4 build.
summary.summary: The tutorial shows how to use OpenCV's EAST text detector, a deep learning model from Zhou et al. (2017), to detect text in natural scene images. It explains why scene text is harder than document text and lists challenges such as blur, lighting, and non-planar surfaces. It then walks through a Python script that resizes the image, runs the network via cv2.dnn, decodes score and geometry maps into boxes, and applies non-maxima suppression from imutils. Results are shown on three sample images, and a second script extends the approach to webcam and video input.
